title: Select-all options stand alone
statement: In a select-all question every option must be decided by the text alone, and finding one right answer must not point to another.
example: Of 1,346 select-all items that had passed structural checks, 0 were usable: the whole pool leaked.
detail: A grade 5 select-all pool was found 100% leaked: none of 1,346 items that had passed structural checks was usable (`grade3-reading/artifacts/alpha-read-packager/generator/g5/MSQ_REGEN_GUIDE.md`, line 3). Its regeneration guide gives the reasons: each option is judged true or false on its own, so world knowledge reaches further than in a single-choice item, and a student who knows one right answer from school can guess the other; the single-choice fixes are necessary but not sufficient (the same file, lines 7-21). It requires every option to rest on a detail of the passage and the right answers not to be paired by theme (the same file, lines 25-42).

evidence.quote: **Status:** MSQ pool is 100% leaked (0 of 1,346 structural-pass items usable).
In MSQ each option is judged true/false independently.
**5. Knowing one correct answer must not help you find the other.**
